newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sept single-family home sales fell 0.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sept single-family home sales fell 0.5 pct.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Department reported sales of new single-family homes, seasonally adjusted, with percent changes from prior months (numbers in 1,000s).
- Pct---Sept Aug--Rev from July--Rev from
-By Region: Pct---Sept Aug--Rev from July--Rev from
Total September sales of single-family homes rose 19.3 percent from an annualized rate of 684,000 units a year ago.
In 1,000s: Sept August--Rev from July--Rev from
Actual Units Sold 65 73 74 66 67
Note-Actual number of new single-family units sold is not seasonally adjusted.
Wall Street economists had expected September single-family home sales at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 768,000 units.
The department also revised monthly percent changes of total sales, seasonally adjusted, from prior months as follows:
- Aug-Rev from July--Rev from June--Rev from
Total Units 4.5 4.7 7.1 8.3 -0.1 Unch
The annualized sales rate for June was revised to 733,000 units from 734,000.
The September supply of homes for sale was 5.2 months' worth, unchanged from August. Previously, the department reported the August supply of homes at 5.3 months' worth.
The inventory of houses for sale at the end of September was 336,000 units, down from a revised 349,000 units in August that was previously reported as 355,000 units.

The September home sales rate was the second highest level since 857,000 in April 1986. The Northeast September sales rate was the highest since April 1993, when it was 102,000 units, the department said.
